topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its interdisciplinary scope, and the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer development and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how accumulating genetic and epigenetic changes cause a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, and how these processes are modeled experimentally.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on tissue invasion, metastatic dissemination, histological progression, and clinical behavior.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions used to classify and name benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the localized and systemic pathophysiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function and cause death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence and mortality patterns of different tumor types across human populations and diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the rationale, histological methods, and relative clinical efficacy of population screening programs across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a recap of the learning outcomes and guidance for upcoming practicals.
